finding_or_summary: Official framework considers individual/collective wellbeing, institutions/governance and wealth of Aotearoa; prompts include distribution, resilience, productivity and sustainability; it is intended to complement other frameworks, including He Ara Waiora and Fonofale.
relevance_and_limit: Contextualises F_001/F_003 and suggests local design constraints; does not validate AURA or CASCADE.

finding_or_summary: CBAx supports consistent, transparent CBA with long-term societal impacts and monetisation where possible; Treasury says results are not evaluated alone and unmonetised impacts/evidence/assumptions also matter.
relevance_and_limit: Strong baseline/comparator for a public-policy tool; warns against a single score deciding policy.

finding_or_summary: UN Statistical Commission adopted SEEA EA in March 2021 as an international statistical standard; framework organises spatial ecosystem data, measures extent/condition/services and links ecosystem change to economic/human activity.
source_type: International statistical standard and technical framework
relevance_and_limit: Closest well-grounded comparator for E_001 ecological accounting. It does not by itself validate tokenisation, financial “eco-linked assets,” or a distinct DEEP protocol.

source_title: Monetary valuation for ecosystem services and assets
finding_or_summary: SEEA material states monetary valuation guidance remains partly interim and under development; monetary accounting is not the only way to represent ecosystem assets/services, which can also be measured physically.
relevance_and_limit: Supports the need for explicit measurement choices and cautions against reducing ecological value to money alone.

source_title: Employee ownership and firm performance: a meta-analysis
finding_or_summary: Meta-analysis of 102 samples representing 56,984 firms found a small positive, statistically significant association between employee ownership and firm performance (reported effect 0.04); authors describe prior empirical results as mixed.
relevance_and_limit: Suggests a potentially positive relationship for a narrower outcome; does not establish lower national Gini, general resilience superiority, or all collaborative models.

source_title: Entry resources and the survival of worker-owned firms
finding_or_summary: French firm cohorts analysis reports apparent worker-owned-firm survival advantage largely dissipates after accounting for entry resources, with a survival advantage remaining in some low-capital/low-knowledge-intensity sectors.
relevance_and_limit: Important counterweight: effects are conditional and confounding/selection matter. Does not support T_001 as a universal law.

finding_or_summary: Survey reviews methods for representing provenance in knowledge graphs, including models and limitations.
relevance_and_limit: Provenance-aware representation is an established research area; Anon Politician should state a specific incremental contribution rather than implying provenance graphs are novel in themselves.

finding_or_summary: OECD describes monitoring/evaluation as important for trustworthy evidence, public accountability and understanding policy performance, trade-offs and impacts.
relevance_and_limit: Supports controlled outcome evaluation and explicit use of evidence; not a validation of the project’s own claims.

source_title: Ideological Alignment and Evidence-Based Policy Adoption
finding_or_summary: A 2026 RCT reported substantially higher adoption when policy information was delivered by institutions ideologically aligned with local policymakers.
relevance_and_limit: Relevant motivation for testing framing/source effects and political symmetry; its context and intervention must not be overgeneralised to all policy decisions.

finding_or_summary: Industry report describes cooperative and mutual business activity and argues it contributes to productivity and community resilience.
relevance_and_limit: Useful NZ descriptive/industry context, but use transparent methods and independent corroboration; do not use advocacy claims alone to validate T_001.

finding_or_summary: Released 5 March 2026; accounts include environmental-protection expenditure (2009–2024, currently experimental), environmental taxes (1999–2024), marine economy (2007–2024), and renewable-energy stock; compiled within the UN SEEA framework.
source_type: Official New Zealand statistical release / metadata
relevance_and_limit: Critical comparator for E_001/DEEP. Confirms substantial existing NZ environmental-economic accounting, while not proving every proposed DEEP function is already covered. Define the remaining gap before building a new protocol.
